_meta.source: live stdio server, dumped via a throwaway MCP client calling session.list_tools() (not written from memory or docs)
_meta.note: This file originally recorded only navigate and snapshot (ticket B1's scope). Ticket B2 added browser_evaluate below, since capture_timetable actually needed it: browser_wait_for (also dumped by B1's --discover-only run) turned out to only support waiting on literal text or a fixed delay, not a CSS selector, so it is not used by capture_timetable and its schema is not recorded here. Fields kept: name, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, annotations - the ones the live server actually populates. Fields dropped: title, icons, _meta, execution - these come back null on every tool in this server's response and are MCP SDK object boilerplate, not server-specific data. The full 24-tool list was confirmed via `python -m agent.run --discover-only`.

notes: no default full-timetable view: nothing renders until a discipline is chosen in the search box
teacher and room are hidden ('Увійдіть, щоб побачити викладачів та аудиторії') unless logged in
group field is course-relative ('гр.1'/'гр.2'), not the institutional BE-3-1 style code
session data is NOT in a <table>: div grid, `.schedule-event-card` inside `.schedule-grid-cell`
the visible week's anchor date is read from <calendar-date value=...>, not from any per-event attribute
confirmed_target_B0.parser: mcp_servers/schedule_mcp/domain/parser.py (_kse_grid_rows, auto-detected when no <table> matches the configured selector)
ticket_B2b_discipline_sweep: Confirmed live against a random sample of 20 codes drawn from the full current-term catalog (api.kse.today's own search endpoint, 188 unique codes found via a 26-query a-z probe - a lower bound, since each query caps at 20 results): roughly half of any given sample have zero sessions in an arbitrary week. A discipline having zero sessions that week is therefore the COMMON case, not an edge case, and PlaywrightTools.capture_full_week must not wait on '.schedule-event-card' itself or it would time out on every one of them.

capture_full_week instead waits for '.schedule-grid-header' (a day-of-week column header) - confirmed always present whenever the grid itself rendered, independent of whether this particular discipline has any sessions, and required unconditionally by _kse_grid_rows too. Once that anchor is confirmed present, whether this discipline has any sessions is decided by counting '.schedule-event-card' elements directly in the captured HTML (not by matching html_to_rows' error text, which would silently misclassify any future rewording of that message as 'no sessions'): zero cards is skipped as a legitimate empty result, and any ToolError html_to_rows does raise when cards ARE present propagates unconditionally, tagged with the discipline code.

Concrete real evidence of within-course multi-session variation across groups/times (see docs/00-execution-plan.md and the B2b PR body for the full example): ECON201 alone has group 1 meeting Mon 08:30-09:50 and Tue 10:30-11:50 (different day, same slot number by coincidence) while group 2 meets Mon 10:30-11:50 and Tue 12:00-13:20 - confirmed against both the committed fixture capture and the underlying api.kse.today/schedule JSON the page itself calls.

browser_snapshot.name: browser_snapshot
browser_snapshot.description: Capture accessibility snapshot of the current page, this is better than screenshot

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

filename.description: Save snapshot to markdown file instead of returning it in the response.

depth.description: Limit the depth of the snapshot tree

boxes.description: Include each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height] in the snapshot. Coordinates are viewport-relative, in CSS pixels (Element.getBoundingClientRect)

browser_evaluate.name: browser_evaluate
browser_evaluate.description: Evaluate JavaScript expression on page or element

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

function.description: () => { /* code */ } or (element) => { /* code */ } when element is provided

filename.description: Filename to save the result to. If not provided, result is returned as text.
